chose: Every HTTP client in file_host and its crates is built by one constructor, outbound::client(Caller), in a new small crate, crates/outbound. Caller is a closed enum with one case per worker (game_feed, call_weeks, cards_essays, mailbox, notice, nudge, health_probe), and a new worker that fetches anything adds a case. Reached inward first (C820): some-metrics owns exposition and not measurement by its own README, and the kits' ReqwestTransports are per-kit adapters. The kits keep their seams and take an outbound::Client. Reached outward (C787): reqwest-middleware does the interception, but its error type wraps reqwest::Error, which would ripple through every caller's error mapping, for a surface of about ten methods. So it is a thin wrapper whose only way onto the wire is Request::send, and it keeps reqwest::Error and reqwest::Response.
options: one constructor in a new small crate, crates/outbound, wrapping reqwest with a closed Caller enum
reqwest-middleware's ClientWithMiddleware with a metrics middleware, Caller carried as an extension
keep each client where it is and add a counter at each of the eight sites
gray: The issue asks for one constructor 'in an existing crate if one fits' but no existing crate owns HTTP: some-metrics' README rules measurement out, and the kits are per-service adapters. reqwest-middleware is the outsourced answer C787 prefers, and the cost against it (its error type rippling through every caller) is a judgement on the size of the ripple, not a rule.
undo: Point the kits' ReqwestTransport back at reqwest::Client, restore the per-site builders and delete crates/outbound; or swap the wrapper for reqwest-middleware behind the same Caller enum.
